# `layerMergeAllWithDependencies`

Detects interdependencies in Layer.mergeAll calls where one layer provides a service that another layer requires

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Anti-pattern |
| Default severity | `warning` |
| Fixable | Yes |
| Effect versions | v3, v4 |
| Diagnostic codes | `TS377035` |
| Language Service name | `layerMergeAllWithDependencies` |
| Oxlint name | `effecttsgo/layer-merge-all-with-dependencies` |

## Preview

```ts
import { Effect, Layer, Context } from "effect"

class A extends Context.Service<A>()("A", { make: Effect.succeed({}) }) {
  static Default = Layer.effect(this, this.make)
}
class B extends Context.Service<B>()("B", { make: Effect.as(A, {}) }) {
  static Default = Layer.effect(this, this.make)
}
export const preview = Layer.mergeAll(A.Default, B.Default)
/**
                                      ^^^^^^^^^ effecttsgo(layer-merge-all-with-dependencies): This layer provides A which is required by another layer in the same Layer.mergeAll call. Layer.mergeAll creates layers in parallel, so dependencies between layers will not be satisfied. Consider moving this layer into a Layer.provideMerge after the Layer.mergeAll.
*/
```
